id: title:Gilbert09:skip github s code frequency stats when a repo exceeds 10k commits

review.posthog_relevance: Adds warehouse ingestion capability to distinguish GitHub API 422 errors caused by repository size limits, allowing recovery or zero-row sync instead of complete ingestion failure.
review.reason: The chunk implements a new exception class, a detection helper, and the raising of that exception in the warehouse ingestion workflow. This establishes a bounded, substantive improvement: it distinguishes a specific transient failure mode (repository too large) from other errors, enabling recovery or graceful degradation rather than complete failure. review.uncertainty: This chunk lacks the caller-side handling and recovery implementation, so the benefit is demonstrated but not fully realized in this group. The tier is assigned based on the implementation and detection, not the recovery. No adoption or incident avoidance is inferred.

observations.limitations: This chunk does not include the implementation of the caller-side handling of GithubRepositoryTooLargeError, only the exception definition, the detection helper, and the test. observations.behavior: Adds GithubRepositoryTooLargeError exception class with documentation explaining GitHub's 10,000-commit endpoint limit.
observations.posthog_connection: Allows warehouse ingestion to distinguish a permanent 422 from transient errors, supporting recovery or zero-row sync.

observations.behavior: Adds helper to detect GitHub 422 responses with the specific 'fewer than 10000 commits' message.
observations.code_quote: return isinstance(message, str) and "fewer than 10000 commits" in message.lower()
observations.posthog_connection: Provides the detection logic for the documented GitHub API behavior, distinguishing this specific 422 from other 422s.

observations.behavior: Adds exception raising in _fetch_page when the repository is too large for code frequency stats.
observations.posthog_connection: Raises the exception to signal the caller that this repository cannot provide code frequency stats, rather than failing the entire warehouse ingestion.
